post.description:
Prices a trip with the same math checkout uses and says whether the vehicle is free. Nothing is saved, so call it as often as you like (120 per minute).

**Body**

- `l_id` (string, required)
- `start`, `end` (string, required) — local times in the listing's timezone
- `extras` (array, optional) — `[{"id": "<extra uuid>", "option": "<option uuid>"}]`. Omit `option` for the first one. Use `with=listings` on `GET /extras` to see what each listing offers. Required extras are always charged; listing one here picks its option.
- `coupon` (string, optional)
- `email` (string, optional) — needed only for coupons limited per customer

**Response**

- `available` — `false` if the vehicle is booked or blocked for those dates (buffer time included)
- `totals` — all in cents: `subtotal`, `discounts`, `taxes`, `total`, `security_deposit`, and `due_at_checkout` (what the renter pays now, per your payment settings)
- `checkout_url` — your storefront's checkout for this listing with the dates filled in. Send the renter there to book and pay; you'll get `reservation.created` when they do.

Delivery isn't priced here yet. Trips that break your booking rules (hours, lead time, trip length) return `422` with the reason under `errors.dates`.

get.description:
Returns bookings (not blocks), newest first, paginated.

**Filters**

- `trip_start` / `trip_end` — trips starting on/after, ending on/before
- `updated_since` — ISO 8601; only bookings changed at or after this moment. Use it to poll incrementally.
- `providers` — comma-separated sources, e.g. `direct,turo`
- `includeAbandoned=true` / `onlyAbandoned=true` — include unfinished checkouts
- `limit` — page size, 1–500 (default 100); follow `links.next` to page
- `include` — comma-separated: `renter`, `listing`, `listingImages`, `vehicle`, `payment`, `rentalAgreement`, `stripeIdentity`

**Trip and payment fields**

- `pickup_location` / `return_location` — where the trip starts and ends: the Turo trip's address, else the delivery address on the order, else the vehicle's branch pickup and return spots
- `odometer_start` / `odometer_end` — readings at pickup and return, typed by the host or captured from a connected car; in the company's distance unit
- `total` — the booked total, in cents
- `amount_paid_in_cents` — what the renter has paid on the order, refundable security deposits excluded; `null` when the booking has no order (Turo trips are paid out by Turo)
- `balance_due_in_cents` — still owed on the order

Amounts are visible only to tokens whose user can view order financials.

**Lookups** (return a single match instead of a list)

- `b_id` — one booking by ID
- `email` or `phone` — a customer's bookings

post.description:
**Scope:** `charges:write`

For a toll or violation service the host connected with an API token: add one toll, violation or fee to a booking. It's billed on the booking's invoices and the host collects it from the renter. If the booking's invoice is already paid, it goes on a new invoice for that booking rather than reopening the paid one. (Services working with many hosts should use the Fleetwire Partner API instead: one key, no per-host tokens.)

- `provider` (string, required) — your service's short id, e.g. `myeztoll` (lowercase letters, digits, `-`, `_`)
- `external_id` (string, required) — your id for the charge. **Idempotent:** sending the same `external_id` with the same amount and kind returns the original with `200` and never bills twice. Different details under the same id return `409`.
- `kind` (required) — `toll`, `violation` or `fee`
- `amount_cents` (integer, required) — the road cost or fine
- `provider_fee_cents` (integer) — your fee, billed as its own line next to the charge
- `occurred_at` (ISO 8601, required except for `fee`) — when the toll was passed or the violation issued
- `description` (string) — shown to the renter on the invoice line, e.g. `E-ZPass NY — 3 tolls, Oct 10`
- `listing_id`, `plate`, `plate_state` — cross-checked against the booking's vehicle
- `authority`, `location`, `citation_number`, `violation_type` (`parking`, `red_light`, `speed`, `other`), `due_at`
- `document` (PDF file, multipart), `document_pdf` (base64) or `document_url` (public https link) — an itemized receipt, up to 5 MB
- `currency` (default `USD`)

**Refused (422)** when the charge isn't for that booking: a different `listing_id` or `plate`, or an `occurred_at` outside the trip. **404** for a booking that isn't yours. **409** when the booking has no order to bill, or the `external_id` conflicts.

`status` is `unbilled`, `billed` (on an unpaid invoice), `paid` or `voided`.

get.description:
Rentals, with no renter details. Two ways to ask:

- **One lookup:** `plate` and `at` return the rental that had that plate at that moment, or an empty list. Optional: if you skip it, Fleetwire matches charges by plate and time itself.
- **A period:** `from` and `to` (at most 93 days apart) return every rental whose trip overlaps the window, paginated, cancelled ones included. Use it for per-rental fees such as a registration fee.

Send one pair or the other, not both. Unconfirmed booking requests are never listed.

post.description:
Send one toll, violation or fee. It's billed on the rental's order by the rental company's own rules.

With `rental_id`, the charge is checked against that rental: the plate must match the rental's vehicle and
`occurred_at` must fall within the trip (with a day either side). If not, you get `422` and nothing is billed.
Without `rental_id`, Fleetwire matches by `plate` and `occurred_at`; if no rental had the car then, the charge
is kept as `unmatched` for the rental company to review.

The receipt can be a multipart file (`document`), base64 (`document_pdf`) or a public `https` link
(`document_url`, downloaded once, no redirects). It must be a PDF of 5 MB or less.

**Idempotent:** the same `external_id` with the same amount and kind returns the original with `200`.
A different amount or kind under the same `external_id` returns `409`; use PATCH to change a charge.
